DES1020.name: The Design Process
DES1020.brief: Design ONE original playable hero for an identified player need. Show three rough ideas, choose one, build it and revise it after tests. Quality and process matter more than making three finished heroes.

outcomes.title: identify the steps in the design process
apply the steps in the design process through production of a designed solution
present a portfolio-ready drawing, rendering or model that the student produced
identify copyright restrictions and permissions and put them into practice
apply consistent and appropriate work station routines
demonstrate basic competencies
make personal connections to the cluster content and processes to inform possible pathway choices

stages.title: Before you build: design brief
stages.prompt: Who is your player? What need or problem will your hero solve? Set three measurable success criteria. Save this before attaching your first prototype.

stages.title: Research & visual language
stages.prompt: Compare two existing heroes or references. Explain what you learned. Identify three elements and two principles of design relevant to your proposed hero.

stages.title: Generate alternatives
stages.prompt: Describe or attach three rough concepts; compare strengths, weaknesses, readability and play style.

stages.title: Choose & plan presentation
stages.prompt: Which idea best meets your criteria? Justify your decision and choose a presentation method and audience.

stages.title: Tools & prototype
stages.prompt: Explain tools/materials selected, their purpose and limitations. Attach a playable hero snapshot and describe how form and function work together.

stages.title: Test, revise, evaluate
stages.prompt: Attach tests or a revised hero. Compare results with your success criteria; identify one improvement and explain the evidence.

stages.title: Portfolio presentation
stages.prompt: Show the work. Add a short caption: one decision, one piece of feedback, and the change you made. Your artifact is the main evidence.

stages.title: Authorship & permissions
stages.prompt: List original work and any borrowed sources. Give creator, licence/permission and changes. A short credit list is enough.

stages.title: Safe work & backups
stages.prompt: Describe posture, breaks, workstation setup and file/version backups. Teacher should observe safe routines; this statement alone is not proof.

stages.title: Skills & collaboration
stages.prompt: Explain a problem you solved using numbers or information. Record partner roles and contributions, or explain your independent responsibilities and how feedback changed your work.

stages.title: Personal pathway
stages.prompt: Connect your interests, strengths and next learning goal to a real occupation. Explain one skill that occupation needs.

ENT1010.name: Challenge & Opportunity
ENT1010.brief: Use the Opportunity Board to compare THREE different customer needs and venture ideas with a weighted decision matrix. Research your ratings, test feasibility and recommend proceed, change or stop. This is opportunity selection, not a full venture plan or campaign comparison. Use the Opportunity Board to compare alternatives and attach its decision matrix; no second feasibility essay is required.

outcomes.title: recognize and assess venture opportunities in their environment
generate ideas for possible venture opportunities in their environment
plan a venture
assess a venture
demonstrate basic competencies
make personal connections to the cluster content and processes to inform possible pathway choices

stages.title: Opportunity scan
stages.prompt: Identify three needs/wants/problems. Use a decision model to compare them and respect different customer perspectives.

stages.title: Generate venture ideas
stages.prompt: Offer three alternatives, conditions/resources needed and how failure can create learning.

stages.title: Outline a venture
stages.prompt: Select an idea. Explain ownership/entry option, rationale, goals, research, resources, market, risk, finances and ethical responsibilities.

stages.title: Feasibility test
stages.prompt: Use the Opportunity Board; attach its decision matrix. Explain where each 0–5 rating and weight came from. Define criteria, resources and timeline; recommend proceed, change or stop. A score based only on assumptions is not real market research.

stages.title: Skills & collaboration
stages.prompt: Explain a problem you solved using numbers or information. Record partner roles and contributions, or explain your independent responsibilities and how feedback changed your work.

stages.title: Personal pathway
stages.prompt: Connect your interests, strengths and next learning goal to a real occupation. Explain one skill that occupation needs.

ENT1020.name: Elements of a Venture Plan
ENT1020.brief: Use the Venture Pilot to plan ONE mining-to-market business. Write a mission, risk and resource plan; compare normal, supplier-delay and demand-drop scenarios, then revise cash, stock and contingency decisions. This is an operations and finance plan, not an opportunity shortlist or advertising experiment. Attach Venture Pilot normal and adverse-scenario reports. The simulation decisions and reports show the planning; add a short critique.

outcomes.title: demonstrate goal-setting and problem-solving strategies that facilitate change
describe potential risks and propose strategies for assessing risks related to a venture
describe strategies for securing resources and support required to implement a venture
select, plan and assess a venture
demonstrate qualities that initiate change
demonstrate basic competencies
make personal connections to the cluster content and processes to inform possible pathway choices

stages.title: Mission & goals
stages.prompt: Set short/long-term goals, mission, ethical policies, legal research and staffing/support network. Distinguish simulation rules from real legal obligations.

stages.title: Risk assessment
stages.prompt: Assess financial, physical and people risks; propose prevention and contingency strategies.

stages.title: Market & resources
stages.prompt: Compare markets/competition and trends. Explain product, target customer, price, place and support/resources required.

stages.title: Venture plan & pilot
stages.prompt: Use the Venture Pilot; attach normal and adverse-scenario reports. Forecast revenue, costs, profit, inventory and cash separately. Outline marketing, production, finance and staffing; choose a reserve and explain how your plan handles risk.

stages.title: Present & revise
stages.prompt: Show the work. Add a short caption: one decision, one piece of feedback, and the change you made. Your artifact is the main evidence.

MAM1010.name: Marketing & Management
MAM1010.brief: Use the Merchandising A/B Lab to compare ONE change for the SAME product and audience. Hold stock and budget constant, interpret units/revenue/profit, then discuss additional pricing, service, place and promotion strategies. This is a controlled retail experiment, not a venture selection or full business plan. Attach a Merchandising A/B Lab comparison. Change one factor and use its results as practical evidence; add a short recommendation.

outcomes.title: identify and describe roles and features within an organization
describe the characteristics of marketing and decisions made within the marketing mix
identify and analyze retail merchandising strategies used in the marketplace today
demonstrate basic competencies
make personal connections to the cluster content and processes to inform possible pathway choices

stages.title: Organization & roles
stages.prompt: Explain planning, organizing, leading, monitoring and communicating. Compare ownership forms and buying/selling/merchandising roles; connect to Canadian retail examples.

stages.title: Marketing mix
stages.prompt: Explain product, price, promotion, place, consumers and competition. Research choices and effects on customers, profit and society.

stages.title: Campaign comparison
stages.prompt: Use the Merchandising A/B Lab and attach a trial. Change ONE factor while holding audience, budget, stock and product constant. Compare pricing, packaging, service/place and promotion strategies beyond the trial; identify model limitations and research real retail examples.

stages.title: Recommendation

CSE1110.name: Structured Programming 1
CSE1110.brief: Write a SEQUENTIAL input → processing → output program in the IPO Workbench. Predict results, translate your algorithm, test success/failure data, debug and revise. Branching and loops are optional extensions, not required for this course.

outcomes.title: demonstrate introductory structured programming skills by writing sequential algorithms to solve problems involving input, processing and output
translate algorithms into source code, convert the source code into machine executable form, execute and debug, as required
analyze and compare the results of the program with the intent of the algorithm and modify as required
demonstrate basic competencies
make personal connections to the cluster content and processes to inform possible pathway choices

stages.title: Algorithm & IPO
stages.prompt: Describe an algorithm and analyze two simple examples. Define your problem, available data, user inputs, processing and outputs. Write pseudocode in the correct sequence before coding.

stages.title: Translate & execute
stages.prompt: Attach an IPO program. Explain editor, translator/interpreter, executor and debugger. Compare an IDE with separate tools; describe variables/constants, data types, literals, assignment/arithmetic and text output. Crossroads interprets bounded instructions; it does not produce a standalone native executable.

stages.title: Predict, test & debug
stages.prompt: Run normal, boundary and failure cases. Record predicted versus actual output, diagnose a syntax/runtime or logic error, revise and retest. Include the saved automated test cases and explain them.

stages.title: Skills & teamwork
stages.prompt: Explain communication, information management, numerical reasoning, responsibility, adaptation, ongoing learning, safe practice and your role in any team.

stages.title: Personal pathway
stages.prompt: Update your interests, skills and resources. Connect this programming experience to an occupation and choose a next learning goal.
